contributions: Overcoming the limitation of inefficient utilization of exploratory diversity caused by isolated evolutionary branches in existing tree-structured evolution paradigms.
Introducing a group-centric evolutionary paradigm that enables explicit experience sharing and reuse within a group during open-ended self-improvement.

Demonstrating significant performance gains and stronger robustness over state-of-the-art open-ended self-evolving methods, with improvements that transfer consistently across different coding models.
limitations: The provided text does not explicitly state limitations of GEA itself, though it notes that existing tree-structured evolution suffers from inefficient utilization of exploratory diversity due to branch isolation—a limitation GEA aims to overcome.
methods: GEA maintains an archive of all discovered agents and operates in two stages per iteration. First, parent group selection uses a Performance-Novelty criterion that balances task performance with evolutionary diversity, computed via cosine distance on task-success vectors. Second, open-ended group evolution allows selected parent agents to jointly produce offspring by sharing a pooled set of evolutionary traces (applied patches, predicted task patches, execution logs, and outcome logs). Each agent reflects on this shared experience, generates framework-level patches through an evolution module, and is evaluated via an action module; successful agents are added to the archive.
results: On SWE-bench Verified, GEA achieves 71.0% success, outperforming the state-of-the-art self-evolving baseline (56.7%) and nearly matching the top human-designed framework OpenHands+GPT-5 (71.8%). On Polyglot, GEA achieves 88.3%, significantly exceeding the baseline (68.3%) and surpassing Aider+GPT-5 (52.0%). GEA also exhibits stronger robustness, fixing framework-level bugs in an average of 1.4 iterations versus 5 for self-evolving methods.
tldr: Group-Evolving Agents (GEA) treats a group of agents as the fundamental evolutionary unit for open-ended self-improvement, enabling explicit experience sharing and reuse across agents to consolidate exploratory diversity into sustained progress. It outperforms state-of-the-art self-evolving methods on coding benchmarks and matches or exceeds top human-designed frameworks without human intervention.
